Oracle Fusion 26B: former opt-ins now standard

Oracle's Current Opt-In Expirations list names 11 features whose opt-in period ended with 26B. They are now standard: 6 are switched on automatically, and 5 need setup if you want to use them. By area: all 11 across Financials, Projects and Supply Chain.

HCM changes are not on this list: Oracle announces them as Redwood default switches. See HCM pages switching to Redwood.

Oracle's note: if you already opted in and finished the setup, nothing changes for you. "Now enabled" and "Oracle's impact" are Oracle's own columns, and the groups below follow Oracle's own Pillar column.

Frequently asked questions

What does "former opt-in now standard" mean in 26B?

Oracle first delivered these features as opt-ins: you had to choose to switch them on. Oracle's Current Opt-In Expirations list names 26B as the update where that opt-in step is removed, so from 26B they are part of the standard product.

How many features stopped being opt-in with 26B?

11, according to Oracle's list. 6 are switched on for all users (Oracle's "Now enabled" column says Yes), and 5 need setup before anyone can use them.

Which modules do the 26B former opt-ins cover?

All 11 across Financials, Projects and Supply Chain.

Do I need to do anything if I already opted in?

No. Oracle says that if you opted in earlier and completed the setup, no further action is needed.

What happens to the 5 features that need setup?

Nothing changes for your users until you do the setup. If you want to use one, follow the steps on its linked Oracle page.

Why are there no HCM features in the 26B list?

Oracle's opt-in expiration list doesn't cover HCM. Oracle announces HCM changes as pages switching to Redwood by default instead. See HCM pages switching to Redwood.
